title: A pre-registered forward test of 86 ZTF periodic-quasar candidates finds no predictive periodicity
summary: The sinusoids of the 86 ZTF periodic-quasar candidates of Chen et al. (2024), frozen on DR11 data, do not predict the next 3.6 years of ZTF data better than red noise or than unselected quasars; none of the three named candidates is confirmed.
abstract: Chen et al. (2024) searched the ZTF DR11 light curves of 143,700 quasars and reported 86 candidates with significant sinusoidal variation against a single power-law red-noise model. Three of them still met the selection criteria in longer archival light curves. A stable sinusoid must continue after the data that found it. We froze the sinusoid of each candidate on the DR11 epochs and scored its prediction of the next 3.6 years of public ZTF r-band data (median 1.42 cycles). We wrote down the test, the controls and the decision rule before we computed any score. Each score was calibrated against damped-random-walk mocks that, in the DR11 window, have a period within 20% of the candidate's and are at least as periodic, up to a cap at ξ = 4. For 14 candidates with too few such mocks, all mocks were used. 7 of 86 candidates beat their mocks at p < 0.05, where chance gives 4.3 (binomial p = 0.139). 29 of 273 magnitude- and redshift-matched quasars that were not selected for periodicity do the same (10.6%; Fisher p = 0.81). None of the three named candidates is confirmed: their p-values are 0.26, 0.81 and 0.40. So we find no evidence that the candidate population continues as strict sinusoids. If all 86 were strict sinusoids at their fitted amplitude, simulations predict 65 passes. At 95% confidence, at most 14% of the candidates are strict sinusoids with the simulated power, or at most 36% with the lower power that we measured by injection into real quasar light curves (post hoc). The test does not exclude quasi-periodic signals, which Chen et al. already proposed as an explanation. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The computations, the code and the text were produced by AI models (from Anthropic and OpenAI), working under the author's direction.
